text: {"lessons":["Taking profits in Stock A and D felt rewarding, but I should base sales on my investment plan and risk—not the satisfaction of locking in gains.","Selling Stock C at a loss hurt, and later selling Stock D below cost also shows that avoiding or realizing a loss is not itself a good reason to trade; I should reassess each holding on its merits.","My account fell over several periods while I mostly did nothing. I should review holdings and diversification regularly, without treating short-term moves as proof of a trend or letting infrequent check-ins replace a plan."]}
